_comment: Tests the AMBIGUOUS CONTINUATION EXCLUSION added to the shared LEAVE MESSAGE block after conv_4501m0rfx5neekqrshdccdtpsbp7 (Karlee Mercuri, 2026-08-24) — caller said 'I'll continue with you' after the CONTACT CLINIC transfer-limitation line and the agent misread it as an affirmative to leave a message, asking 'What would you like me to pass on?' with nothing to pass on.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous continuation after CONTACT CLINIC offer — must clarify, not assume LEAVE MESSAGE

history.content: Can I speak to the receptionist, please?
I'm not able to transfer your call to reception, but I can pass on a message for them to call you back.
I'll continue with you.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent asks a clarifying question such as 'Sure — would you like me to pass on a message, or is there something else I can help with?' (or a very close equivalent), with zero tool call this turn. FAIL if: agent asks 'What would you like me to pass on?' or otherwise proceeds into the LEAVE MESSAGE MESSAGE STEP; FAIL if: agent calls universal_router intent='leave_message' this turn — the caller never confirmed they want a message left, 'I'll continue with you' only means they are not hanging up.

scenarios.name: Genuine affirmative after CONTACT CLINIC offer — must still fire LEAVE MESSAGE (regression control)

history.content: Can I speak to the receptionist, please?
I'm not able to transfer your call to reception, but I can pass on a message for them to call you back.
Yes please.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent proceeds into the LEAVE MESSAGE MESSAGE STEP by asking 'What would you like me to pass on?' with zero tool call this turn. FAIL if: agent treats 'Yes please' as ambiguous and asks a clarifying question instead — the AMBIGUOUS CONTINUATION EXCLUSION must not over-fire on a genuine affirmative.

scenarios.name: Cancel intent stated in the same message as a speak-to-person request — must cancel directly, not offer a callback (conv_2801m1j6hjehf93sn6jnhgwhxaa0, Jane So, 2026-09-02)

history.content: Hi Jane! How can I help you today?

I have an appointment with Bruce Sutton tomorrow afternoon. I'd like to cancel that appointment because my husband has been taken to hospital, and I don't know what'll be happening. Can I speak to a person, please?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent does NOT say 'I'm not able to transfer your call to reception' or any transfer-limitation line this turn; agent instead speaks a brief acknowledgement (an empathy phrase or one of the SIGNAL 2B polite acks) AND calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' in the same turn (called_number, caller_id, payload including timeframe_raw='tomorrow afternoon' if captured) with zero confirmation question first. FAIL if: agent fires the CONTACT CLINIC transfer-limitation line; FAIL if: agent asks 'would you like me to cancel that?' or any confirmation question instead of executing immediately; FAIL if: agent produces zero tool call this turn; FAIL if: agent calls universal_router with intent='leave_message' or intent='callback_request' instead of intent='cancel_intent'.

scenarios.name: Reschedule intent stated in the same message as a speak-to-person request — must reschedule directly, not offer a callback (regression control)

history.content: Hi Jane! How can I help you today?
I need to reschedule my appointment tomorrow to a different day — is there someone I could talk to about it?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent does NOT say 'I'm not able to transfer your call to reception' or any transfer-limitation line this turn; agent instead speaks a brief polite ack AND calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' with reschedule_mode='true' in the same turn, with zero confirmation question first. FAIL if: agent fires the CONTACT CLINIC transfer-limitation line; FAIL if: agent calls intent='cancel_intent' without reschedule_mode='true'; FAIL if: agent produces zero tool call this turn.

scenarios.name: Pure speak-to-person request, no cancel/reschedule/booking content — CONTACT CLINIC must still fire (regression control)

history.content: Hi Jane! How can I help you today?
Can I speak to a person, please?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent says 'I'm not able to transfer your call to reception, but I can pass on a message for them to call you back.' (or a very close equivalent), with zero tool call this turn. FAIL if: agent calls universal_router with intent='cancel_intent' or intent='book_intent' — there is no cancel/reschedule/booking content in this message, so the new EXCLUSION must not over-fire and suppress the normal CONTACT CLINIC response.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name + caller confirms without stating name — must ASK, not assume/echo

history.content: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths. May I ask your name please?
Yeah, that's me — you've got it on file.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent does NOT say 'Hi John' or otherwise address the caller by {{caller_first_name}}, does not set patient_name_stated, and explicitly asks for the caller's name (e.g. 'May I ask your name please?' or a very close equivalent), with zero tool call this turn. FAIL if: agent greets the caller as 'John' (or any pre-set name) without the caller having explicitly stated it this call, or proceeds to route a signal using the assumed name.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name matches + caller explicitly states their name while booking — capture normally (regression control)

history.content: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths. May I ask your name please?
It's John — I'd like to book an appointment.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent treats 'It's John' as an explicit stated name (patient_name_raw='John', patient_name_stated='true') and, because booking language is also present, fires SIGNAL 1 BOOKING INTENT — spoken ack (e.g. 'Hi John!') immediately followed by a universal_router intent='book_intent' tool call in the same turn. FAIL if: agent asks for the name again despite it being explicitly stated this turn, or fails to call universal_router with intent='book_intent'.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name + caller states a different name — NAME SAVE FLOW must still trigger (regression control)

history.content: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths. May I ask your name please?
This is Sarah.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent sets phone_owner_denied='true', patient_name_raw='Sarah', and runs NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 1 — speaking something equivalent to 'Hi Sarah! I have this number saved under John — should I update your patient record to Sarah for future calls and bookings?' with zero tool calls this turn. FAIL if: agent assumes the caller is John, greets them as John, or skips straight into NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 2 / routing without the STEP 1 confirmation question.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name + caller states first name plus surname (first word matches) — capture normally, no NAME SAVE FLOW

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Lorna Tyson.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent treats 'Lorna Tyson' as the same caller giving their surname — sets patient_name_raw='Lorna Tyson', patient_name_stated='true', does NOT set phone_owner_denied, and does NOT run NAME SAVE FLOW (no 'I have this number saved under Lorna — should I update your patient record' question). Agent should proceed normally, e.g. greeting 'Hi Lorna Tyson! How can I help you today?' and waiting, or routing directly if booking/other intent language is also present. FAIL if: agent asks 'should I update your patient record to Lorna Tyson' or otherwise runs NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 1 — the first word of the stated name ('Lorna') matches {{caller_first_name}} ('Lorna'), so this is not a different name.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name + caller states an unrelated full name (first word does not match) — NAME SAVE FLOW must still trigger (regression control)

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Sarah Tyson.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent sets phone_owner_denied='true', patient_name_raw='Sarah Tyson', and runs NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 1 — speaking something equivalent to 'Hi Sarah Tyson! I have this number saved under Lorna — should I update your patient record to Sarah Tyson for future calls and bookings?' with zero tool calls this turn. FAIL if: agent treats 'Sarah Tyson' as matching {{caller_first_name}} ('Lorna') and skips NAME SAVE FLOW — the first word 'Sarah' does not match 'Lorna', so the surname-match exclusion must NOT apply here.

scenarios.name: Pre-set caller_first_name + surname-match with a name NOT in either worked example — generalization probe

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Margaret Chen.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent treats 'Margaret Chen' as the same caller giving their surname — sets patient_name_raw='Margaret Chen', patient_name_stated='true', does NOT set phone_owner_denied, and does NOT run NAME SAVE FLOW (no 'I have this number saved under Margaret — should I update your patient record' question). Neither 'Margaret' nor 'Chen' appears in this node's worked examples ('Lorna Tyson', 'Roslyn Newcomen') — this scenario specifically tests whether the 'compare ONLY the first word' rule generalizes beyond the two memorized examples, not just pattern-matches them. FAIL if: agent asks 'should I update your patient record to Margaret Chen' or otherwise runs NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 1.

scenarios.name: details_ack already in-flight (found, zero appointments) — compound question must not re-trigger the appointment message or re-call details_ack

history.content: Do I have an appointment on Thursday at 3, and also do I need a referral to see Bruce?
Let me check that.
{"intent": "details", "message": "You do not have any upcoming appointments. Would you like to book one?", "patient_lookup_done": "true", "appointment_lookup_failed": ""}
You do not have any upcoming appointments. Would you like to book one?
{"status": "in_progress", "message": "Executing the task in the background. Result will be reported later."}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: the agent's next turn does NOT repeat or paraphrase the appointment message ('you do not have any upcoming appointments...') again, does NOT call details_ack a second time (a details_ack call already exists in history for this details result, only in_progress rather than completed — DETAILS_ACK CALL LOCK treats that the same as completed), and instead addresses the still-unanswered second half of the caller's original message (the referral question) via ordinary node logic — e.g. a filler phrase plus a universal_router intent='info_pivot' call, or an equivalent in-scope routing call. FAIL if: the agent re-speaks the appointment/no-appointments message in whole or in part; FAIL if: the agent calls details_ack again; FAIL if: the agent calls universal_router intent='details' again; FAIL if: the agent goes silent and does nothing about the referral question.

scenarios.name: details_ack already in-flight (not-found) — compound question must not re-fire the silent ack a second time

history.content: Can you check if I have an appointment Thursday, and also what is your address?
One moment.

{"intent": "details", "message": "I could not find your details in our system. Have you booked with us before?", "error": "patient_not_found", "patient_lookup_done": "true", "appointment_lookup_failed": "true", "appointment_lookup_intent": "details"}
{"status": "in_progress", "message": "Executing the task in the background. Result will be reported later."}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: the agent's next turn does NOT call details_ack again (a call for this result already exists in history, only in_progress rather than completed — DETAILS_ACK CALL LOCK treats that the same as completed) and does NOT speak the not-found message or ask 'have you booked with us before' again — this node never speaks about a failed lookup, and appointment_lookup_failed='true' already routes automatically via an expression edge to the appointment-lookup-recovery node, so the caller's address question does not need to be answered here either. Silence / no further tool call this turn is an acceptable PASS. FAIL if: the agent calls details_ack again; FAIL if: the agent speaks the not-found message or any paraphrase of it; FAIL if: the agent calls universal_router intent='details' again.

scenarios.name: NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 2 YES, no original intent — must produce zero tool calls this turn

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Michael Grant.
Hi Michael Grant! I have this number saved under Roslyn — should I update your patient record to Michael Grant for future calls and bookings?
Yes.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent speaks exactly 'Hi Michael Grant! How can I help you today?' (or a very close equivalent) as this turn's entire output, with ZERO tool calls this turn — no universal_router call of any kind, including intent='save_caller_name'. The save_caller_name payload is deferred to whichever universal_router call fires on a later turn. FAIL if: the agent calls universal_router (with intent='save_caller_name' or any other intent) in this same turn — even if the spoken line is also correct, any tool call this turn is a FAIL, because it triggers a dynamic-variable update that causes this same line to be spoken a second time on the following turn (the exact bug from a live call, conv_9401m1fxbd2de4zbpt4rnvrq7r01, 2026-09-02).

scenarios.name: NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 2 NO, no original intent — must produce zero tool calls this turn

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Michael Grant.
Hi Michael Grant! I have this number saved under Roslyn — should I update your patient record to Michael Grant for future calls and bookings?
No, that's fine.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent speaks exactly 'No problem! How can I help you today?' (or a very close equivalent) as this turn's entire output, with ZERO tool calls this turn — no universal_router call of any kind. FAIL if: the agent calls universal_router in this same turn — this duplicates the greeting on the next turn via the same mid-turn DV-update mechanism as the YES branch.

scenarios.name: Fresh caller states full name, no intent yet — greeting must use first name only

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Robyn Coben.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent speaks 'Hi Robyn! How can I help you today?' (or a very close equivalent using ONLY the first name 'Robyn'), with ZERO tool calls this turn. FAIL if: the agent speaks the full stated name back, e.g. 'Hi Robyn Coben!' — the caller's surname must never be spoken aloud in the greeting, only used internally in patient_name_raw for the payload.

scenarios.name: NAME SAVE FLOW STEP 1 — mismatch greeting must use first name only

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?
Michael Grant.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent's spoken greeting starts with 'Hi Michael!' (first name only) — e.g. 'Hi Michael! I have this number saved under Roslyn — should I update your patient record to Michael Grant for future calls and bookings?' — note the record-update question may still name the full 'Michael Grant' since that is confirming what to save, not a spoken greeting. FAIL if: the greeting itself says 'Hi Michael Grant!' using the full stated name.

scenarios.name: Practitioner availability question misread as own-appointment lookup (conv_0401m1gangjtfhatycema9kxn3zg, Barbara Liepins, 2026-09-02)

history.content: How lovely to hear from you, Barbara! How can I help you today?
I was wondering if Elisa might have an appointment for tomorrow.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent fires SIGNAL 1 (BOOKING INTENT) — one gentle ack (e.g. 'Lovely!') then a universal_router intent='book_intent' tool call in the same turn, with practitioner_preference set to Elisa (or 'Elisa Brownhill') and timeframe_raw='tomorrow' in the payload. FAIL if: agent fires SIGNAL 2 (APPOINTMENT LOOKUP, intent='details') or any appointment-lookup dispatch — this is a live incident where the agent told the caller 'You don't have any upcoming appointments. Would you like to book one?' in response to this exact message, ignoring that she had just asked about a NEW booking with a named practitioner, not her own existing booking.

scenarios.name: Genuine own-appointment check — must still fire SIGNAL 2, not booking intent (regression control)

history.content: How lovely to hear from you, Barbara! How can I help you today?
I'm just checking, do I have an appointment coming up?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent fires SIGNAL 2 (APPOINTMENT LOOKUP) — the caller is asking about their OWN existing booking in first person ('do I have'), with no practitioner named. FAIL if: agent fires SIGNAL 1 (book_intent) or any new-booking routing — the new practitioner-availability carve-out must not swallow a genuine first-person appointment check that names no practitioner.

scenarios.name: Attendee substitution on existing appointment — must route Signal 2B cancel_intent, not details/leave_message

history.content: You've reached Raymond Terrace and Tea Gardens Osteopaths, you're speaking with AI Jane. This call is recorded. May I ask your name please?.
Diane Stevens.
Hi Diane! How can I help you today?
I, uh, have an appointment tomorrow, um, but I'm unable to come, but my sister-in-law is coming, Fran Mitchell, in place of me.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent speaks one polite ack (e.g. 'Of course.') AND calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' with reschedule_mode='true' and family_member_name='Fran Mitchell' in the same turn (Signal 2B, ATTENDEE SUBSTITUTION). FAIL if: agent calls universal_router intent='details' (this is not a plain appointment lookup); FAIL if: agent offers to leave a message for the clinic or calls intent='leave_message' instead of resolving it directly; FAIL if: family_member_name is omitted from the payload.

scenarios.name: Attendee substitution phrased without cancel/reschedule words — must still fire Signal 2B

history.content: Hi John! How can I help you today?
My appointment on Friday — can my wife Karen come in my place instead?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' with reschedule_mode='true' and family_member_name='Karen' (Signal 2B). FAIL if: agent treats this as a plain lookup (intent='details') or asks a clarifying/confirmation question first (NO CONFIRMATION QUESTION rule) — this signal executes immediately.

scenarios.name: Practitioner named as OBJECT of 'to see' inside a 'do you have' availability question misread as own-appointment lookup (conv_1501m23des5pf4xsgy77g03ykyzq, Vaughan Sullivan, 2026-09-10)

history.content: Hi Vaughan! How can I help you today?
Do you have appointment early this morning to see Elise?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent fires SIGNAL 1 (BOOKING INTENT) — one gentle ack (e.g. 'Lovely!') then a universal_router intent='book_intent' tool call in the same turn, with practitioner_preference set to Elise (or 'Elisa Brownhill') and timeframe_raw capturing 'early this morning' in the payload. FAIL if: agent fires SIGNAL 2 (APPOINTMENT LOOKUP, intent='details') or any appointment-lookup dispatch — this is a live incident where the agent told the caller 'You have two upcoming appointments...' in response to this exact message, misreading the 'do you have ... to see Elise' availability question (practitioner named as the OBJECT of 'to see', not the subject) as a lookup of the caller's own existing booking. The earlier practitioner-availability-not-appointment-lookup fix only covered the practitioner-as-SUBJECT phrasing ('I was wondering if Elisa might have an appointment') and missed this OBJECT-position phrasing.

scenarios.name: Practitioner named as OBJECT of 'with' (not 'to see') inside a 'do you have' availability question — preposition-variant regression control

history.content: Hi Sarah! How can I help you today?
Do you have an appointment on Friday with Dr Smith?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent fires SIGNAL 1 (BOOKING INTENT) — one gentle ack then a universal_router intent='book_intent' tool call in the same turn, with practitioner_preference set to Dr Smith and timeframe_raw capturing 'Friday' in the payload. FAIL if: agent fires SIGNAL 2 (APPOINTMENT LOOKUP) — the object-position fix must cover both the 'to see' and 'with' prepositions, not just the 'to see' phrasing from the original live incident.

scenarios.name: LEAVE MESSAGE with caller_id null — must ask for a callback number before executing, not proceed straight to the tool call

history.content: I'm not feeling great today — can you let them know I won't be in and ask them to call me back?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent extracts message_body from this turn (CONTEXT SCAN), skips MESSAGE STEP and NAME STEP (name already known), then — because {{caller_id}} is empty — fires the CALLBACK NUMBER GATE: asks something equivalent to 'And what's the best number to reach you on?' with ZERO tool calls this turn, and HALTs. FAIL if: agent calls universal_router intent='leave_message' this turn without first collecting a callback number; FAIL if: agent instead asks a 'just to confirm — is that right?' recap of the message content — no such confirmation step exists in this flow, only the callback-number question.

scenarios.name: LEAVE MESSAGE with caller_id already set — must skip the callback number question and execute directly, no invented confirmation

history.content: I'm not feeling great today — can you let them know I won't be in and ask them to call me back?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent skips the CALLBACK NUMBER GATE entirely (caller_id is already set) and goes straight to EXECUTE — one filler phrase from the TOOL-CALL FILLER set, then a universal_router intent='leave_message' tool call in the SAME turn, with no callback-number question and no 'just to confirm — is that right?' recap of the message content first. FAIL if: agent asks for a phone number (caller_id is already set, this question is unnecessary); FAIL if: agent asks any confirmation/recap question and stops without calling the tool in the same or an immediately-following turn with no intervening caller reply.

scenarios.name: LEAVE MESSAGE, caller_id null, caller has just given the requested callback number — must execute now, with the stated number in payload

history.content: I'm not feeling great today — can you let them know I won't be in and ask them to call me back?
And what's the best number to reach you on?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if: agent proceeds directly to EXECUTE in this turn — one filler phrase, then universal_router intent='leave_message' with the payload including a phone number field (e.g. caller_phone) set to '0412 345 678', plus caller_name and message_body from the original turn. FAIL if: agent asks the callback-number question again; FAIL if: agent asks any further confirmation ('is that right?') before calling the tool; FAIL if: the tool call omits the caller-stated phone number entirely, leaving the clinic with no way to call the patient back.
